etymologies.etymologyHTML: Genericized trademark of German Aspirin, from acetylierte Spirsäure (literally “acetylated spiraeic acid”). The trade name Aspirin is a registered trademark in some countries, but has entered the English language in generic usage, as various German trademarks were nullified in the United States after World War I (see also heroin).

definitions.definition: (uncountable, organic chemistry, pharmacology) an analgesic drug, acetylsalicylic acid

quote.citation: 1936, F.J. Thwaites, The Redemption, Sydney: H. John Edwards Publishing, published 1940, page 107:
quote.text: "It nearly drove me insane. I took heaven alone knows how many aspirins."
